title: VibeJVMBench submission result
description: One file at jvms/<target-name>/<timestamp>.json: everything one bench run (bench/run.py and/or bench/mc/run.py) measured for one target JVM/toolchain build. schema_version 1.

target.description: Identity of the JVM/toolchain under test

name.description: Matches the jvms/<name>/ directory this file lives under.

version.description: Free-text build identity: a git commit, release tag, or similar. Not used for sorting/filtering, only display/provenance.

is_java_launcher.description: True iff measured with --target-is-java: target is a plain java-style launcher, not a compiler/packager built from source for this run.

reference_jdks.description: Per reference engine (g1/zgc/graal), the contents of that JDK's release file.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC. The *filename* this is saved under must be colon-free, e.g. 2026-10-17T17-43-00Z.json; this field keeps the normal colon-bearing ISO-8601 form.

harness_commit.description: Free-text provenance for the benchmark harness itself (e.g. a git commit of the VibeJVMBench repo), not the target.

run.description: The invocation that produced the mc/ scenarios below, if any (bench/mc/run.py §9.4).

scenarios.description: scenario-name -> scenario. Current scenario names from: worldgen, tick, datagen, upgrade. New scenario names may appear without a schema change.

startup_ms.description: bench/run.py §6.8: median wall-clock process-start latency, 5 samples, lower_is_better always true.

vs_hotspot.description: bench/run.py results relative to HotSpot G1 measured in the same run on the same machine. This, not raw timings, is what the results site compares across submissions.

groups.description: Geometric mean per benchmark group (main, vector, runtime, real, suites) plus micro (main+vector+runtime).

benchmarks.description: benchmark-name -> relative, for every benchmark where both target and HotSpot G1 succeeded.

harness.description: Optional: bench/run.py's own microbenchmark/suite results for this target, reusing results.json shape verbatim (not re-specified here).

relative.description: Target performance relative to HotSpot G1 measured in the same run on the same machine. ratio > 1 (pct > 0) always means the target did better, whichever direction the underlying metric runs: hotspot/target for lower-is-better metrics, target/hotspot for higher-is-better ones.

n.description: For geometric means: how many ratios were combined.

metric.description: One statistically-summarized metric: rig.summarize() over an engine's successful per-run samples.

n.description: Successful sample count feeding this metric.

samples.description: Optional raw per-run values, for transparency/re-analysis. May be omitted for large sample counts.

verdict.description: rig.verdict() of this submission's target against a named reference baseline for one metric.

baseline.description: Which reference engine this target was compared to, e.g. hotspot-g1, hotspot-zgc, graal.

win.description: True iff the target's confidence interval clears the baseline's median entirely.

scenario.description: One bench/mc scenario's results for the target, plus however many reference engines were also run in the same invocation.

failed_runs.description: Count of this scenario's runs that errored for the target.

target_metrics.description: metric-name -> metric, for the target engine. Metric names are scenario-specific and open-ended; every scenario also carries exit, rss_mb, gc_pauses, gc_pause_max_ms, gc_pause_total_ms, gc_full_pauses, gc_full_pause_max_ms from ended()).

reference_metrics.description: reference-engine-name -> (metric-name -> metric), for whichever of hotspot-g1/hotspot-zgc/graal/target-base were also measured in this invocation.

verdicts.description: metric-name -> verdict, for metrics where a baseline comparison was computed.

vs_hotspot.description: metric-name -> target median relative to the hotspot-g1 median from this same invocation; what the results site compares.
